Package com.bilt.pos.session

Class Terminal

java.lang.Object
com.bilt.pos.session.Terminal
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public final class Terminal extends Object implements AutoCloseable
A terminal's device and admin operations — diagnostics, totals, reconciliation, printing, sound — outside any session.

These map to SERVICE/DEVICE-class nexo messages that carry no session reference on the wire, so unlike a CheckoutSession there is no bracket: build() sends nothing, and the terminal holds no state on this object's behalf. Use it for a connectivity ping before the first checkout, end-of-day reconciliation with no customer present, or a receipt reprint after the session that took the payment has ended.

Operations are lazy like every session operation: methods returning a SessionResult send nothing until execute(), executeSync(), get(), or getOrNull() is invoked. Asynchronous executions run one at a time on the terminal's own operation thread and deliver their handlers through the configured callbackExecutor, with the same semantics as the session builders.


 Terminal terminal = Terminal.builder()
         .client(client)
         .saleId("POS-LANE-3")
         .poiId("VictaLane-275839164")
         .build();

 terminal.diagnose()
         .onSuccess(d -> register.showTerminalStatus(d.getPoiStatus()))
         .onError(e -> register.showUnreachable(e.getMessage()))
         .execute();

close() sends nothing — there is nothing to end on the terminal — it only stops this object accepting further operations. Mid-checkout, CheckoutSession.terminal() keeps these operations one call away.

    • close

      public void close()
      Stops accepting operations. Sends nothing — the terminal holds no state for this object, so there is nothing to end — and is idempotent. Operations executed after this fail with SessionErrorCode.INVALID_STATE through their normal onError/onComplete delivery.
      Specified by:
      close in interface AutoCloseable
